name: Random.__init__
reason: pyInit is self.seed(x) on the tp_new state, then gauss_next = None (:125-126); InitMatchesSeed makes Random(x) equal r.seed(x) on any valid r, value or exception, so an __init__ that did not seed fails. self.seed is bound to Random.seed: a subclass seed override (a documented hook, :110-111) is outside the model.

name: Random.seed
reason: seedConvert/pySeed mirror :146-174 (the v1 latin-1 hash, the v2 str/bytes/bytearray SHA-512 int, the TypeError, then super().seed), but no entry says what reaches super().seed: SeedStrBytesAgree and the str/bytes half of SeedV1Hash are equalities between seed calls, SeedV2AllBits and the range half of SeedV1Hash are about the helpers alone, and SeedAllOrNothing/InitMatchesSeed hold of any seed, so a seed that seeded every argument with 0 passes all six.

name: Random.getstate
reason: pyGetstate is (VERSION, super().getstate(), gauss_next) (:178) over the C mirror cGetstate; StateRoundTrip makes setstate(getstate()) restore the object exactly at every point of the stream, so a lossy getstate fails.

name: Random.setstate
reason: pySetstate keeps :182-200 in order: state[0], the version-3 and version-2 unpacking that assigns gauss_next before the C call, x % 2**32 with ValueError -> TypeError, the C tuple, size and range checks, and the version ValueError; StateRoundTrip, SetstateVersions and SetstateFailureKeepsCore pin it, and the SetstateAtomic refutation is sound (probe: gauss_next is 9.5 after a rejected (3, (1,)*3, 9.5)).

name: Random.__getstate__
reason: The body is return self.getstate() (:214), and its only statement is the PickleRoundTrip conjunct pyDunderGetstate o = pyReduce o, where both are pyGetstate by definition: an alias restated as rfl. Unpickling never calls it (__reduce__ is defined, :210-212).

name: Random.__setstate__
reason: pyDunderSetstate is self.setstate(state) (:217); PickleRoundTrip runs it inside pyUnpickle and needs it to restore the object over a freshly seeded instance, so a no-op __setstate__ fails (the SetstateVersions alias conjunct adds nothing).

name: Random.__reduce__
reason: pyReduce is the getstate() part of (self.__class__, (), self.getstate()) (:220); PickleRoundTrip, whatever entropy the fresh instance reads, gives back the object, so a reduce that lost state fails. The class element is taken as a constant, so a subclass's class is not checked.

name: Random.__init_subclass__
reason: initSubclass is the MRO loop of :234-243 with its in-class order _randbelow > getrandbits > random; InitSubclassPick pins the first deciding class and termination on an MRO holding Random. (The method also drops **kwargs without chaining to super(); see the report.)

name: Random._randbelow_with_getrandbits
reason: randbelowWith mirrors the k = n.bit_length() draw and the rejection loop (:248-252), but RandbelowInRange only says the result is < n (and a fact about 2**bit_length), which always-0 also satisfies; the withdrawal stands.

name: Random._randbelow_without_getrandbits
reason: randbelowWithout mirrors both branches (:260-272) over an abstract Flt, not Binary64; RandbelowWithoutInRange is range-only for n < 2**53 (always 0 passes), and the n >= 2**53 bound is the open entry rand-randbelow-without-huge.

name: Random.randbytes
reason: randbytes is n * 8, self.getrandbits on a fallible Gen, then to_bytes(n, 'little') (:289); RandbytesSpec, for every valid generator, makes the result exactly the n little-endian bytes of that same draw and propagates its exception, so a constant or reordered result fails.

name: Random.randrange
reason: randrange mirrors :304-333 (index of start, `step is not _ONE`, the fast path, the length formula, the zero-step and empty-range errors with their f-string text and the 4300-digit limit); RandrangeIsRangeChoice is exactly one _randbelow(L) and range(...)[j], so it pins the mapping, and RandrangeArgErrors pins the rejections. IntArg has no user __index__ object; one would only change str() in a message.

name: Random.randint
reason: randint mirrors _index(a), _index(b), the b < a ValueError and a + _randbelow(b - a + 1) (:339-342); RandintSpec makes it equal randrange(a, b+1) call for call, plus the ValueError and the range.

name: Random.choice
reason: choice mirrors the two len() calls and seq[_randbelow(len)] (:352-354), but ChoiceSpec is membership (seq[j] for some j in range), which always seq[0] satisfies; the withdrawal stands.

name: Random.shuffle
reason: shuffleLoop mirrors the reversed(range(1, len(x))) swap loop (:359-363), but ShuffleSpec says only that the result is a permutation and does not raise, and ShuffleImmutable is the TypeError after one draw; the identity permutation passes both, so the withdrawal stands.

name: Random.sample
reason: sample mirrors the Sequence check, the counts branch (accumulate, pop, the total checks, bisect), setsize and both loops (:420-458); but SampleDistinctPositions is positions only and SampleCountsEquivalent is a twin that "always the first k" also satisfies, and the negative-counts refutation (probe: counts=[3, -1] gives ['a', 'a']) runs only the total < 0 check.

name: Random.choices
reason: choices mirrors the plain, weights and cum_weights branches and their errors (:466-495) over an abstract Flt, not Binary64; ChoicesSpec is k items each population[j] with k draws, which always population[0] satisfies. The in-range claim is the open entry rand-choices-index-in-range.

name: Random.uniform
reason: Floats are the abstract Flt class (Lean Float in the difftest, no Binary64 instance), and OneDraw says only that one random() is used, so any function of that draw passes; the range claim is the open entry rand-uniform-range.

name: Random.triangular
reason: Draw count only (OneDraw), over an abstract Flt rather than Binary64: any function of the one draw passes, including on the ZeroDivisionError path.

name: Random.normalvariate

name: Random.binomialvariate
reason: BinomialEdges pins n < 0, p == 0 -> 0, p == 1 -> n and one draw for n == 1, but nothing on the BG/BTRS paths, so any whole-draw function passes there. The NaN refutation is sound (probe: binomialvariate(5, nan) raises AssertionError, binomialvariate(1, nan) gives 0) but runs on NanF, and the range claim is the open entry rand-binomial-range.
